endpoint.title: List brands
endpoint.description: Returns every brand, as a plain array (no pagination). The seeded data has two brands. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Create brand
endpoint.description: Creates a brand. No token is needed (see Notes). _(source)_

201.schemaRaw: Brand

endpoint.title: Get brand
endpoint.description: Returns one brand. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Update brand
endpoint.description: Updates a brand with the fields sent. No token is needed (see Notes). Despite being `PUT`, no field is required, and the slug has no uniqueness rule: a duplicate is caught by the database instead. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Partially update brand
endpoint.description: Updates only the validated fields that are sent (`$request->validated()`). _(source)_

endpoint.title: Delete brand
endpoint.description: Deletes a brand. Admin only. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Search brands
endpoint.description: Searches brand names. Queries of 4 characters or more use a MySQL full-text prefix match (`MATCH(name) AGAINST('<q>*' IN BOOLEAN MODE)`); shorter ones use `LIKE '%<q>%'`. _(source)_ A missing `q` returns every brand, not an error. _(verified)_

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. The spec marks it required, but without it the API returns `200` with all brands.

200.schemaRaw: Brand[]   // empty array when nothing matches

endpoint.title: Search brands (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /brands/search`, with the criteria in a JSON body (RFC 10008 `QUERY` method); the body keys are merged into the query string. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Create cart
endpoint.description: Creates an empty cart and returns its id. The optional coordinates are stored on the cart and later decide the location discount of the items added to it. Nothing is validated. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Add item to cart
endpoint.description: Adds a product to the cart. When the product is already in the cart, its quantity is **increased** by `quantity` (`firstOrCreate` + `increment`); no second line is created (1 + 2 = 3, 99 + 99 = 198). _(verified)_ The service's own test adds 2 to an item with quantity 1 and expects 3. _(source)_

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: The cart's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Get cart
endpoint.description: Returns the cart with its items, each with its product. For an item with a non-zero `discount_percentage`, `discounted_price` is added: the product price minus the discount, rounded to 2 decimals. _(source)_

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: The cart's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Update item quantity
endpoint.description: Sets (replaces) the quantity of a product that is in the cart. _(source)_

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: The cart's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Remove product from cart
endpoint.description: Deletes the cart's line for this product and recalculates the cart's combined (rental + product) discount. _(source)_

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: The product's id (not the cart item's id)

endpoint.title: List categories
endpoint.description: Returns every category, top-level and sub-categories alike, as a flat array without `sub_categories` (no pagination). The seeded data has 19 categories: 3 top-level and 16 sub-categories. _(verified)_

200.schemaRaw: Category[]   // keys id, name, slug, parent_id

endpoint.title: Create category
endpoint.description: Creates a category; with `parent_id` it becomes a sub-category of that category. No token is needed (see Notes). _(source)_

201.schemaRaw: Category   // the created model: the fields sent plus id; parent_id appears only when it was sent

endpoint.title: Get category tree
endpoint.description: Returns the top-level categories (`parent_id` is `null`), each with its `sub_categories`, loaded recursively (the seeded data has two levels, so sub-categories have an empty `sub_categories`). _(verified)_

parameters.name: by_category_slug
parameters.description: Only the top-level category with this slug. A sub-category's slug or an unknown slug returns `[]`.

200.schemaRaw: CategoryTree[]   // 3 items unfiltered, 1 or 0 with by_category_slug

endpoint.title: Get category tree (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /categories/tree`, with the criteria in a JSON body (RFC 10008 `QUERY` method); the body keys are merged into the query string. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Get category
endpoint.description: Returns one category, top-level or sub-category, with its `sub_categories` (recursive). A sub-category comes back with its `parent_id` and an empty `sub_categories`. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Search categories
endpoint.description: Searches category names, across top-level and sub-categories; each result has its `sub_categories` loaded. Queries of 4 characters or more use a MySQL full-text prefix match (`MATCH(name) AGAINST('<q>*' IN BOOLEAN MODE)`); shorter ones use `LIKE '%<q>%'`. _(source)_ A missing `q` returns every category, not an error. _(verified)_

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. The spec marks it required, but without it the API returns `200` with all 19 categories.

200.schemaRaw: CategoryTree[]   // empty array when nothing matches

endpoint.title: Search categories (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /categories/search`, with the criteria in a JSON body (RFC 10008 `QUERY` method); the body keys are merged into the query string. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Update category
endpoint.description: Updates a category with the fields sent. No token is needed (see Notes). Despite being `PUT`, no field is required, and the slug has no uniqueness rule: a duplicate is caught by the database instead. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Partially update category
endpoint.description: Updates only the validated fields that are sent (`$request->validated()`). _(source)_

endpoint.title: Delete category
endpoint.description: Deletes a category. Admin only. _(source)_

endpoint.title: List favorites
endpoint.description: Returns all favorites of the user of the token, each with its product and the product's image. The list isn't paginated. An empty list is `[]`. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Add favorite
endpoint.description: Adds a product to the favorites of the user of the token. `user_id` is always taken from the token; any other field in the body is ignored (only `user_id` and `product_id` are fillable). _(source)_

201.schemaRaw: Favorite   // see Data Models; without the product

endpoint.title: Get favorite
endpoint.description: Returns one favorite by id, without its product. _(source)_

parameters.name: favoriteId
parameters.description: The favorite's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Delete favorite
endpoint.description: Removes the favorite with this id if it belongs to the user of the token. _(source)_

parameters.name: favoriteId
parameters.description: The favorite's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: List images
endpoint.description: Returns every row of the `product_images` table as a JSON array. The list is not paginated, filtered or sorted by the API: `index()` returns `ProductImage::all()`. _(source)_ An empty table gives `[]`. _(source)_

endpoint.title: List invoices
endpoint.description: Returns a page of invoices, newest `invoice_date` first, 15 per page. An admin gets every invoice (guest invoices included); any other user gets only the invoices whose `user_id` is theirs. Each item has its lines (with a slim product and its image) and the payment method. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Search invoices
endpoint.description: Searches the invoices visible to the caller (own, or all for an admin) with a `LIKE '%q%'` on `invoice_number`, `billing_street` and `status`. Same page shape and ordering as the list. _(source)_

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search phrase. The spec marks it required; the code doesn't, and without it the pattern is `%%`, which matches every invoice visible to the caller. `%` and `_` in `q` aren't escaped. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Search invoices (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /invoices/search`, but the criteria are sent as a JSON body (RFC 10008 `QUERY` method). The `query.body` middleware merges the body keys into the query string, so the results equal the `GET` with the same parameters. The response carries the header `Accept-Query: application/json`. _(source)_ The header was seen on the `401` of this endpoint. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Get invoice
endpoint.description: Returns one invoice with its lines (each with the product, its image, category and brand) and its payment with the payment details. _(source)_

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Download invoice PDF
endpoint.description: Downloads the PDF generated for an invoice number. The path value is the invoice's number (for example `INV-2022000002`), not its id. A scheduled job generates the files (see Notes). _(source)_

endpoint.title: Get PDF generation status
endpoint.description: Returns the status of the PDF job for an invoice number, from the `downloads` table. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Update invoice status
endpoint.description: Sets the `status` and/or `status_message` of an invoice. Any logged-in user can do it for any invoice (see Notes). _(source)_

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Create invoice
endpoint.description: Creates an invoice for the user of the token from a cart, with one line per cart item, the totals and the payment, and queues the checkout email and the stock update. `user_id` comes from the token and `invoice_date` is set to the current time (a sent `invoice_date` is validated but not used). _(source)_

requestBody.schemaRaw:
{
  payment_method: PaymentMethod;     // see Enums
  payment_details: PaymentDetails;   // the key must be present; fields depend on the method (see Data Models)
  billing_street: string;            // max 70
  billing_city: string;              // max 40
  billing_state?: string;            // max 40; the spec marks it required
  billing_country: string;           // max 40, e.g. "NL"; checked against the postal code, city and state
  billing_postal_code?: string;      // max 10; the spec marks it required
  invoice_date?: string;             // Y-m-d; accepted, but the invoice gets the current time
  cart_id: string;                   // required; an existing cart
}

201.schemaRaw: InvoiceCreated   // see Data Models

endpoint.title: Create guest invoice
endpoint.description: Same as `POST /invoices`, without a token: the invoice has `user_id: null`, so only an admin can read it afterwards. The guest's email and names are used for the checkout email only; they are not stored on the invoice. _(source)_

requestBody.schemaRaw:
{
  payment_method: PaymentMethod;     // see Enums
  payment_details: PaymentDetails;   // the key must be present; see Data Models
  billing_street: string;            // max 70
  billing_city: string;              // max 40
  billing_state?: string;            // max 40
  billing_country: string;           // max 40; checked against the postal code, city and state
  billing_postal_code?: string;      // max 10
  invoice_date?: string;             // Y-m-d; accepted, but the invoice gets the current time
  cart_id: string;                   // required; an existing cart
  guest_email: string;               // valid email, max 255
  guest_first_name: string;          // max 255
  guest_last_name: string;           // max 255
}

201.schemaRaw: InvoiceCreated   // see Data Models

endpoint.title: Update invoice
endpoint.description: Updates an invoice of the caller. The body is validated like a new invoice (so the payment and cart fields are required although they aren't used), then every `fillable` key of the body is written to the invoice. The invoice must belong to the token's user: an admin can't update other users' invoices either. _(source)_

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's id (named `{id}` in the route)

requestBody.schemaRaw:
{
  payment_method: PaymentMethod;     // required by the validation, not stored
  payment_details: PaymentDetails;   // the key must be present, not stored; gift card format rules apply
  billing_street: string;            // max 70
  billing_city: string;              // max 40
  billing_state?: string;            // max 40
  billing_country: string;           // max 40; checked against the postal code, city and state
  billing_postal_code?: string;      // max 10
  invoice_date?: string;             // Y-m-d
  cart_id: string;                   // required by the validation, not stored
}

endpoint.title: Partially update invoice
endpoint.description: Updates the billing address or the date of an invoice of the caller. Only the validated keys are written. _(source)_

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's id (named `{id}` in the route)

requestBody.schemaRaw:
{
  billing_street?: string;        // max 70
  billing_city?: string;          // max 40
  billing_state?: string;         // max 40
  billing_country?: string;       // max 40; no address-versus-country check here
  billing_postal_code?: string;   // max 10
  invoice_date?: string;          // Y-m-d
  cart_id?: string;               // validated and then ignored (not fillable)
}

endpoint.title: List messages
endpoint.description: Returns a page of contact messages, newest `created_at` first, 15 per page. An admin gets every message, each with its sender (`user`, `null` for a guest message); any other user gets only the messages whose `user_id` is theirs, without the `user` relation. There is no filter or search. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Send message
endpoint.description: Stores a contact message with status `NEW`. Guests and logged-in users can send one. With a valid token the message gets the token's `user_id` and shows up in that user's list; without a token it has no owner. The deployed API runs with `APP_ENV=production` (`GET /status` reports `"environment": "production"`), so no email is queued: the service queues the mail only when the environment is `local`. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: ContactMessage   // see Data Models: the created message, not { success: true } as the spec says

endpoint.title: Get message
endpoint.description: Returns one message with its sender and its replies (each reply with its author). An admin can read any message; any other user only their own. _(source)_

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Reply to message
endpoint.description: Adds a reply to a message and sets the message to `IN_PROGRESS` first, whatever its current status. The reply's author is the token's user. There is no role check and no ownership check, so any logged-in user can reply to any message (see Notes). _(source)_

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id (named `{id}` in the route)

201.schemaRaw: ContactReply   // see Data Models

endpoint.title: Attach file to message
endpoint.description: Checks a file uploaded for a message. The service only validates the upload and logs it: **nothing is stored and the message id is never looked up**, so the call answers the same for an unknown id. The only upload that succeeds is an empty `.txt` file. Needs no token. _(source)_

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id (named `{id}` in the route); not checked for existence

endpoint.title: Update message status
endpoint.description: Sets the status of a message to `NEW`, `IN_PROGRESS` or `RESOLVED`. There is no state machine: any status can be set from any other, including the same one. There is no role check and no ownership check. _(source)_

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Check payment
endpoint.description:
Validates the details of the chosen payment method and answers `200` with `{ message: "Payment was successful" }` when they pass. Only the method named in `payment_method` is validated, and all of its fields are validated together, so a `422` lists every failing field. Nothing is stored. _(verified)_

The check runs only for the five exact values in Enums. For any other `payment_method` (a different case such as `"Bank Transfer"`, an unknown string, an array, or none) and for an empty body, nothing is validated and the answer is `200`. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Look up an address by postcode
endpoint.description: Returns an address for the given country and postcode. The locality (`street`, `city`, `state`) depends only on the country and the postcode (case-insensitive), not on the house number, so the same input always gives the same locality. `house_number` is echoed when sent and generated otherwise. `country` and `postcode` come back in upper case. _(verified)_

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country code, such as `NL`. At most 40 characters (41 gives `422`). _(verified)_

parameters.name: postcode
parameters.description: Postcode. At most 10 characters (11 gives `422`); must fit the country's format when the country has a known one. _(verified)_

parameters.name: house_number
parameters.description: House number. At most 10 characters (11 gives `422`). An empty value counts as omitted. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: List a product's specs
endpoint.description: Returns the specs of one product as a plain array (no pagination). An id that matches no product returns an empty array, not `404`. _(verified)_ A product without specs does the same _(verified)_, because the query only filters on `product_id` _(source)_.

200.schemaRaw: ProductSpec[]   // [] when the product has no specs or doesn't exist

endpoint.title: Add a spec to a product
endpoint.description: Creates a spec for the product in the path. The product isn't looked up first. _(source)_

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Product ULID. Must exist (see the `500` below).

201.schemaRaw: ProductSpec   // { product_id, spec_name, spec_value, spec_unit, id }; spec_unit is null when not sent

endpoint.title: Get a spec
endpoint.description: Returns one spec, looked up by its id within the product in the path. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Update a spec
endpoint.description: Updates the fields that are sent. Despite being `PUT`, no field is required: an empty body `{}` passes validation and changes nothing. The spec is looked up by id within the product in the path. _(verified)_

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Product ULID of the product that owns the spec

endpoint.title: Delete a spec
endpoint.description: Deletes a spec of the product in the path. It answers `204` also when nothing was deleted. _(verified)_

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Product ULID of the product that owns the spec

endpoint.title: List spec names
endpoint.description: Returns every distinct spec name with its distinct values and one unit, across all products. The names and values are the ones `by_spec` on `GET /products` filters on (`name:value1|value2`, see `Products_API.md`). _(verified)_

endpoint.title: List products
endpoint.description: Returns the products, 9 per page. Without `is_rental`, rental products are excluded (`is_rental` defaults to false). _(verified)_

parameters.name: by_brand
parameters.description: Brand id, or several ids separated by commas

parameters.name: by_category
parameters.description: Category id, or several ids separated by commas

parameters.name: by_category_slug
parameters.description: Category slug; also matches its direct sub-categories. In the source, not in the spec.

parameters.name: is_rental
parameters.description: true` or `1` returns only rentals; anything else, or no value, returns only non-rentals

parameters.name: eco_friendly
parameters.description: true` or `1`: only products with CO2 rating A or B. In the source, not in the spec.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Name contains this text. In the source, not in the spec.

endpoint.title: List products (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /products`, but the criteria are sent as a JSON body (RFC 10008 `QUERY` method). The body keys are merged into the query string, so the results equal the `GET` with the same parameters. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Create product
endpoint.description: Creates a product. No token is needed (see Notes). _(source)_

201.schemaRaw: Product   // with product_image, category and brand loaded

endpoint.title: Get product
endpoint.description: Returns one product with its category (including `parent_id`), brand, image and specs. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Update product
endpoint.description: Updates a product with the fields sent. No token is needed (see Notes). Despite being `PUT`, no field is required. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Partially update product
endpoint.description: Updates only the validated fields that are sent. Unlike `PUT`, fields without a rule (`co2_rating`, `stock`) are dropped. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Delete product
endpoint.description: Deletes a product. Admin only. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Get related products
endpoint.description: Returns up to 10 other products from the same category as the given product. _(verified)_

200.schemaRaw: Array<Omit<Product, 'co2_rating'>>   // category has id and name only; no co2_rating field

endpoint.title: Search products
endpoint.description: Searches product names. Returns 9 per page. Special characters are stripped from `q`; an empty or missing `q` returns an empty page, not an error. _(verified)_

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. The spec marks it required, but without it the API returns `200` with an empty `data` array.

endpoint.title: Search products (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /products/search`, with the criteria in a JSON body. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Total sales of years
endpoint.description: Returns the summed `total` of the `COMPLETED` invoices per year, from `current year - years` up to and including the current year, oldest first. Years without invoices are in the list with `total: 0`, so the list has `years + 1` items. _(source)_

parameters.name: years
parameters.description: How many years before the current one to include. Default `1` (the current and the previous year). `0` gives only the current year; a negative value gives `[]`. The code doesn't validate it. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: TotalSalesOfYearsRow[]   // see Data Models; years + 1 items, ascending by year

endpoint.title: Total sales per country
endpoint.description: Returns the summed invoice `total` of the `COMPLETED` invoices, grouped by `billing_country`. Only countries that have such invoices appear, so the list can be empty. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: TotalSalesPerCountryRow[]   // see Data Models; no fixed length, no explicit order

endpoint.title: Top 10 purchased products
endpoint.description: Returns up to ten products by the number of invoice lines that reference a product with that name, highest first. It counts lines, not quantities, over invoices of every status, and groups by product name. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: TopPurchasedProductRow[]   // see Data Models; at most 10 items, descending by count

endpoint.title: Top 10 best selling categories
endpoint.description: Returns up to ten categories with the highest sum of `unit_price` over the invoice lines of their products, highest first. The sum ignores quantity and discounts and covers invoices of every status. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: TopSellingCategoryRow[]   // see Data Models; at most 10 items, descending by total_earned

endpoint.title: Customers by country
endpoint.description: Returns the number of users with the `user` role per `country`. Admins are not counted; disabled customers are. _(source)_ A row with `country: null` was seen in the live body _(verified)_; it groups the customers registered without a country, which registration allows _(source)_.

200.schemaRaw: CustomersByCountryRow[]   // see Data Models; no fixed length, no explicit order

endpoint.title: Average sales per month
endpoint.description: Returns, for each month of one year, the average `total` and the number of `COMPLETED` invoices. The list always has 12 items for the months 1 to 12; months without invoices have `average: 0` and `amount: 0`. _(source)_

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: The year to report on. Default: the current year. The spec says the default is `2022`. The code doesn't validate it. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: AverageSalesPerMonthRow[]   // see Data Models; always 12 items, month 1 to 12

endpoint.title: Average sales per week
endpoint.description: Returns, for each week of one year, the average `total` and the number of `COMPLETED` invoices. The list always has 52 items for the weeks 1 to 52; weeks without invoices have `average: 0` and `amount: 0`. _(source)_

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: The year to report on. Default: the current year. The spec says the default is `2022`. The code doesn't validate it. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: AverageSalesPerWeekRow[]   // see Data Models; always 52 items, week 1 to 52

endpoint.title: Login
endpoint.description: Returns a JWT for the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Accounts with two-factor auth (TOTP) get a restricted temporary token instead, which is exchanged for a full token by sending it back with the TOTP code. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Register
endpoint.description: Creates a customer account (role `user`). _(source)_

endpoint.title: Forgot password
endpoint.description: Sets the account's password to `welcome02`. No email confirmation or token is involved. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Change password
endpoint.description: Changes the current user's password. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Current user
endpoint.description: Profile of the user the token belongs to. `role`, `enabled` and `failed_login_attempts` are returned only when the caller is an admin. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Logout
endpoint.description: Invalidates (blacklists) the token. Later requests with it get `401`. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Refresh token
endpoint.description: Returns a new token for the one in the `Authorization` header and invalidates the old one. An expired token can still be refreshed within the refresh window (`JWT_REFRESH_TTL`, 60 minutes by default). This route has no auth middleware; the token is read by the handler. _(source)_

endpoint.title: List users
endpoint.description: Lists customer accounts (role `user` only), 15 per page. Admin only. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Search users
endpoint.description: Searches customer accounts (role `user` only) by first name, last name, email and city. Any logged-in user can search (see Notes). Returns 15 per page. _(source)_

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. The spec marks it required; without it every customer matches.

endpoint.title: Search users (HTTP QUERY)

endpoint.title: Get user
endpoint.description: Returns a user. A non-admin can only get their own record. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Update user
endpoint.description: Updates a user's profile. A non-admin can only update their own record; only an admin can send `role`. `password` is ignored (use change-password). _(source)_

endpoint.title: Partially update user
endpoint.description: Updates only the validated fields that are sent. A non-admin can only patch their own record. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Delete user
endpoint.description: Deletes a user. Admin only. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Create cart
endpoint.description: Creates an empty cart and returns its id. The optional coordinates are stored on the cart and later decide the location discount of the items added to it. Nothing is validated. _(source)_

When the product is already in the cart, its quantity is **increased** by `quantity` (`firstOrCreate` + `increment`); no second line is created (1 + 2 = 3, 99 + 99 = 198). _(verified)_ The service's own test adds 2 to an item with quantity 1 and expects 3. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Get cart
endpoint.description: Returns the cart with its items, each with its product. For an item with a non-zero `discount_percentage`, `discounted_price` is added: the product price minus the discount, rounded to 2 decimals. _(source)_

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: The cart's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Update item quantity
endpoint.description: Sets (replaces) the quantity of a product that is in the cart. _(source)_

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: The cart's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Remove product from cart
endpoint.description: Deletes the cart's line for this product and recalculates the cart's combined (rental + product) discount. _(source)_

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: The product's id (not the cart item's id)

endpoint.title: List categories
endpoint.description: Returns every category, top-level and sub-categories alike, as a flat array without `sub_categories` (no pagination). The seeded data has 19 categories: 3 top-level and 16 sub-categories. _(verified)_

200.schemaRaw: Category[]   // keys id, name, slug, parent_id

endpoint.title: Create category
endpoint.description: Creates a category; with `parent_id` it becomes a sub-category of that category. No token is needed (see Notes). _(source)_

201.schemaRaw: Category   // the created model: the fields sent plus id; parent_id appears only when it was sent

endpoint.title: Get category tree
endpoint.description: Returns the top-level categories (`parent_id` is `null`), each with its `sub_categories`, loaded recursively (the seeded data has two levels, so sub-categories have an empty `sub_categories`). _(verified)_

parameters.name: by_category_slug
parameters.description: Only the top-level category with this slug. A sub-category's slug or an unknown slug returns `[]`.

200.schemaRaw: CategoryTree[]   // 3 items unfiltered, 1 or 0 with by_category_slug

endpoint.title: Get category tree (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /categories/tree`, with the criteria in a JSON body (RFC 10008 `QUERY` method); the body keys are merged into the query string. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Get category
endpoint.description: Returns one category, top-level or sub-category, with its `sub_categories` (recursive). A sub-category comes back with its `parent_id` and an empty `sub_categories`. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Search categories
endpoint.description: Searches category names, across top-level and sub-categories; each result has its `sub_categories` loaded. Queries of 4 characters or more use a MySQL full-text prefix match (`MATCH(name) AGAINST('<q>*' IN BOOLEAN MODE)`); shorter ones use `LIKE '%<q>%'`. _(source)_ A missing `q` returns every category, not an error. _(verified)_

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. The spec marks it required, but without it the API returns `200` with all 19 categories.

200.schemaRaw: CategoryTree[]   // empty array when nothing matches

endpoint.title: Search categories (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /categories/search`, with the criteria in a JSON body (RFC 10008 `QUERY` method); the body keys are merged into the query string. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Update category
endpoint.description: Updates a category with the fields sent. No token is needed (see Notes). Despite being `PUT`, no field is required, and the slug has no uniqueness rule: a duplicate is caught by the database instead. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Partially update category
endpoint.description: Updates only the validated fields that are sent (`$request->validated()`). _(source)_

endpoint.title: Delete category
endpoint.description: Deletes a category. Admin only. _(source)_

endpoint.title: List favorites
endpoint.description: Returns all favorites of the user of the token, each with its product and the product's image. The list isn't paginated. An empty list is `[]`. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Add favorite
endpoint.description: Adds a product to the favorites of the user of the token. `user_id` is always taken from the token; any other field in the body is ignored (only `user_id` and `product_id` are fillable). _(source)_

201.schemaRaw: Favorite   // see Data Models; without the product

endpoint.title: Get favorite
endpoint.description: Returns one favorite by id, without its product. _(source)_

parameters.name: favoriteId
parameters.description: The favorite's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Delete favorite
endpoint.description: Removes the favorite with this id if it belongs to the user of the token. _(source)_

parameters.name: favoriteId
parameters.description: The favorite's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: List images
endpoint.description: Returns every row of the `product_images` table as a JSON array. The list is not paginated, filtered or sorted by the API: `index()` returns `ProductImage::all()`. _(source)_ An empty table gives `[]`. _(source)_

endpoint.title: List invoices
endpoint.description: Returns a page of invoices, newest `invoice_date` first, 15 per page. An admin gets every invoice (guest invoices included); any other user gets only the invoices whose `user_id` is theirs. Each item has its lines (with a slim product and its image) and the payment method. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Search invoices
endpoint.description: Searches the invoices visible to the caller (own, or all for an admin) with a `LIKE '%q%'` on `invoice_number`, `billing_street` and `status`. Same page shape and ordering as the list. _(source)_

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search phrase. The spec marks it required; the code doesn't, and without it the pattern is `%%`, which matches every invoice visible to the caller. `%` and `_` in `q` aren't escaped. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Search invoices (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /invoices/search`, but the criteria are sent as a JSON body (RFC 10008 `QUERY` method). The `query.body` middleware merges the body keys into the query string, so the results equal the `GET` with the same parameters. The response carries the header `Accept-Query: application/json`. _(source)_ The header was seen on the `401` of this endpoint. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Get invoice
endpoint.description: Returns one invoice with its lines (each with the product, its image, category and brand) and its payment with the payment details. _(source)_

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Download invoice PDF
endpoint.description: Downloads the PDF generated for an invoice number. The path value is the invoice's number (for example `INV-2022000002`), not its id. A scheduled job generates the files (see Notes). _(source)_

endpoint.title: Get PDF generation status
endpoint.description: Returns the status of the PDF job for an invoice number, from the `downloads` table. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Update invoice status
endpoint.description: Sets the `status` and/or `status_message` of an invoice. Any logged-in user can do it for any invoice (see Notes). _(source)_

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Create invoice
endpoint.description: Creates an invoice for the user of the token from a cart, with one line per cart item, the totals and the payment, and queues the checkout email and the stock update. `user_id` comes from the token and `invoice_date` is set to the current time (a sent `invoice_date` is validated but not used). _(source)_

requestBody.schemaRaw:
{
  payment_method: PaymentMethod;     // see Enums
  payment_details: PaymentDetails;   // the key must be present; fields depend on the method (see Data Models)
  billing_street: string;            // max 70
  billing_city: string;              // max 40
  billing_state?: string;            // max 40; the spec marks it required
  billing_country: string;           // max 40, e.g. "NL"; checked against the postal code, city and state
  billing_postal_code?: string;      // max 10; the spec marks it required
  invoice_date?: string;             // Y-m-d; accepted, but the invoice gets the current time
  cart_id: string;                   // required; an existing cart
}

201.schemaRaw: InvoiceCreated   // see Data Models

endpoint.title: Create guest invoice
endpoint.description: Same as `POST /invoices`, without a token: the invoice has `user_id: null`, so only an admin can read it afterwards. The guest's email and names are used for the checkout email only; they are not stored on the invoice. _(source)_

requestBody.schemaRaw:
{
  payment_method: PaymentMethod;     // see Enums
  payment_details: PaymentDetails;   // the key must be present; see Data Models
  billing_street: string;            // max 70
  billing_city: string;              // max 40
  billing_state?: string;            // max 40
  billing_country: string;           // max 40; checked against the postal code, city and state
  billing_postal_code?: string;      // max 10
  invoice_date?: string;             // Y-m-d; accepted, but the invoice gets the current time
  cart_id: string;                   // required; an existing cart
  guest_email: string;               // valid email, max 255
  guest_first_name: string;          // max 255
  guest_last_name: string;           // max 255
}

201.schemaRaw: InvoiceCreated   // see Data Models

endpoint.title: Update invoice
endpoint.description: Updates an invoice of the caller. The body is validated like a new invoice (so the payment and cart fields are required although they aren't used), then every `fillable` key of the body is written to the invoice. The invoice must belong to the token's user: an admin can't update other users' invoices either. _(source)_

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's id (named `{id}` in the route)

requestBody.schemaRaw:
{
  payment_method: PaymentMethod;     // required by the validation, not stored
  payment_details: PaymentDetails;   // the key must be present, not stored; gift card format rules apply
  billing_street: string;            // max 70
  billing_city: string;              // max 40
  billing_state?: string;            // max 40
  billing_country: string;           // max 40; checked against the postal code, city and state
  billing_postal_code?: string;      // max 10
  invoice_date?: string;             // Y-m-d
  cart_id: string;                   // required by the validation, not stored
}

endpoint.title: Partially update invoice
endpoint.description: Updates the billing address or the date of an invoice of the caller. Only the validated keys are written. _(source)_

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description: The invoice's id (named `{id}` in the route)

requestBody.schemaRaw:
{
  billing_street?: string;        // max 70
  billing_city?: string;          // max 40
  billing_state?: string;         // max 40
  billing_country?: string;       // max 40; no address-versus-country check here
  billing_postal_code?: string;   // max 10
  invoice_date?: string;          // Y-m-d
  cart_id?: string;               // validated and then ignored (not fillable)
}

endpoint.title: List messages
endpoint.description: Returns a page of contact messages, newest `created_at` first, 15 per page. An admin gets every message, each with its sender (`user`, `null` for a guest message); any other user gets only the messages whose `user_id` is theirs, without the `user` relation. There is no filter or search. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Send message
endpoint.description: Stores a contact message with status `NEW`. Guests and logged-in users can send one. With a valid token the message gets the token's `user_id` and shows up in that user's list; without a token it has no owner. The deployed API runs with `APP_ENV=production` (`GET /status` reports `"environment": "production"`), so no email is queued: the service queues the mail only when the environment is `local`. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: ContactMessage   // see Data Models: the created message, not { success: true } as the spec says

endpoint.title: Get message
endpoint.description: Returns one message with its sender and its replies (each reply with its author). An admin can read any message; any other user only their own. _(source)_

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Reply to message
endpoint.description: Adds a reply to a message and sets the message to `IN_PROGRESS` first, whatever its current status. The reply's author is the token's user. There is no role check and no ownership check, so any logged-in user can reply to any message (see Notes). _(source)_

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id (named `{id}` in the route)

201.schemaRaw: ContactReply   // see Data Models

endpoint.title: Attach file to message
endpoint.description: Checks a file uploaded for a message. The service only validates the upload and logs it: **nothing is stored and the message id is never looked up**, so the call answers the same for an unknown id. The only upload that succeeds is an empty `.txt` file. Needs no token. _(source)_

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id (named `{id}` in the route); not checked for existence

endpoint.title: Update message status
endpoint.description: Sets the status of a message to `NEW`, `IN_PROGRESS` or `RESOLVED`. There is no state machine: any status can be set from any other, including the same one. There is no role check and no ownership check. _(source)_

parameters.name: messageId
parameters.description: The message's id (named `{id}` in the route)

endpoint.title: Check payment
endpoint.description:
Validates the details of the chosen payment method and answers `200` with `{ message: "Payment was successful" }` when they pass. Only the method named in `payment_method` is validated, and all of its fields are validated together, so a `422` lists every failing field. Nothing is stored. _(verified)_

The check runs only for the five exact values in Enums. For any other `payment_method` (a different case such as `"Bank Transfer"`, an unknown string, an array, or none) and for an empty body, nothing is validated and the answer is `200`. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Look up an address by postcode
endpoint.description: Returns an address for the given country and postcode. The locality (`street`, `city`, `state`) depends only on the country and the postcode (case-insensitive), not on the house number, so the same input always gives the same locality. `house_number` is echoed when sent and generated otherwise. `country` and `postcode` come back in upper case. _(verified)_

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Country code, such as `NL`. At most 40 characters (41 gives `422`). _(verified)_

parameters.name: postcode
parameters.description: Postcode. At most 10 characters (11 gives `422`); must fit the country's format when the country has a known one. _(verified)_

parameters.name: house_number
parameters.description: House number. At most 10 characters (11 gives `422`). An empty value counts as omitted. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: List a product's specs
endpoint.description: Returns the specs of one product as a plain array (no pagination). An id that matches no product returns an empty array, not `404`. _(verified)_ A product without specs does the same _(verified)_, because the query only filters on `product_id` _(source)_.

200.schemaRaw: ProductSpec[]   // [] when the product has no specs or doesn't exist

endpoint.title: Add a spec to a product
endpoint.description: Creates a spec for the product in the path. The product isn't looked up first. _(source)_

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Product ULID. Must exist (see the `500` below).

201.schemaRaw: ProductSpec   // { product_id, spec_name, spec_value, spec_unit, id }; spec_unit is null when not sent

endpoint.title: Get a spec
endpoint.description: Returns one spec, looked up by its id within the product in the path. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Update a spec
endpoint.description: Updates the fields that are sent. Despite being `PUT`, no field is required: an empty body `{}` passes validation and changes nothing. The spec is looked up by id within the product in the path. _(verified)_

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Product ULID of the product that owns the spec

endpoint.title: Delete a spec
endpoint.description: Deletes a spec of the product in the path. It answers `204` also when nothing was deleted. _(verified)_

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Product ULID of the product that owns the spec

endpoint.title: List spec names
endpoint.description: Returns every distinct spec name with its distinct values and one unit, across all products. The names and values are the ones `by_spec` on `GET /products` filters on (`name:value1|value2`, see `Products_API.md`). _(verified)_

endpoint.title: List products
endpoint.description: Returns the products, 9 per page. Without `is_rental`, rental products are excluded (`is_rental` defaults to false). _(verified)_

parameters.name: by_brand
parameters.description: Brand id, or several ids separated by commas

parameters.name: by_category
parameters.description: Category id, or several ids separated by commas

parameters.name: by_category_slug
parameters.description: Category slug; also matches its direct sub-categories. In the source, not in the spec.

parameters.name: is_rental
parameters.description: true` or `1` returns only rentals; anything else, or no value, returns only non-rentals

parameters.name: eco_friendly
parameters.description: true` or `1`: only products with CO2 rating A or B. In the source, not in the spec.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Name contains this text. In the source, not in the spec.

endpoint.title: List products (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /products`, but the criteria are sent as a JSON body (RFC 10008 `QUERY` method). The body keys are merged into the query string, so the results equal the `GET` with the same parameters. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Create product
endpoint.description: Creates a product. No token is needed (see Notes). _(source)_

201.schemaRaw: Product   // with product_image, category and brand loaded

endpoint.title: Get product
endpoint.description: Returns one product with its category (including `parent_id`), brand, image and specs. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Update product
endpoint.description: Updates a product with the fields sent. No token is needed (see Notes). Despite being `PUT`, no field is required. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Partially update product
endpoint.description: Updates only the validated fields that are sent. Unlike `PUT`, fields without a rule (`co2_rating`, `stock`) are dropped. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Delete product
endpoint.description: Deletes a product. Admin only. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Get related products
endpoint.description: Returns up to 10 other products from the same category as the given product. _(verified)_

200.schemaRaw: Array<Omit<Product, 'co2_rating'>>   // category has id and name only; no co2_rating field

endpoint.title: Search products
endpoint.description: Searches product names. Returns 9 per page. Special characters are stripped from `q`; an empty or missing `q` returns an empty page, not an error. _(verified)_

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. The spec marks it required, but without it the API returns `200` with an empty `data` array.

endpoint.title: Search products (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /products/search`, with the criteria in a JSON body. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Total sales of years
endpoint.description: Returns the summed `total` of the `COMPLETED` invoices per year, from `current year - years` up to and including the current year, oldest first. Years without invoices are in the list with `total: 0`, so the list has `years + 1` items. _(source)_

parameters.name: years
parameters.description: How many years before the current one to include. Default `1` (the current and the previous year). `0` gives only the current year; a negative value gives `[]`. The code doesn't validate it. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: TotalSalesOfYearsRow[]   // see Data Models; years + 1 items, ascending by year

endpoint.title: Total sales per country
endpoint.description: Returns the summed invoice `total` of the `COMPLETED` invoices, grouped by `billing_country`. Only countries that have such invoices appear, so the list can be empty. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: TotalSalesPerCountryRow[]   // see Data Models; no fixed length, no explicit order

endpoint.title: Top 10 purchased products
endpoint.description: Returns up to ten products by the number of invoice lines that reference a product with that name, highest first. It counts lines, not quantities, over invoices of every status, and groups by product name. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: TopPurchasedProductRow[]   // see Data Models; at most 10 items, descending by count

endpoint.title: Top 10 best selling categories
endpoint.description: Returns up to ten categories with the highest sum of `unit_price` over the invoice lines of their products, highest first. The sum ignores quantity and discounts and covers invoices of every status. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: TopSellingCategoryRow[]   // see Data Models; at most 10 items, descending by total_earned

endpoint.title: Customers by country
endpoint.description: Returns the number of users with the `user` role per `country`. Admins are not counted; disabled customers are. _(source)_ A row with `country: null` was seen in the live body _(verified)_; it groups the customers registered without a country, which registration allows _(source)_.

200.schemaRaw: CustomersByCountryRow[]   // see Data Models; no fixed length, no explicit order

endpoint.title: Average sales per month
endpoint.description: Returns, for each month of one year, the average `total` and the number of `COMPLETED` invoices. The list always has 12 items for the months 1 to 12; months without invoices have `average: 0` and `amount: 0`. _(source)_

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: The year to report on. Default: the current year. The spec says the default is `2022`. The code doesn't validate it. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: AverageSalesPerMonthRow[]   // see Data Models; always 12 items, month 1 to 12

endpoint.title: Average sales per week
endpoint.description: Returns, for each week of one year, the average `total` and the number of `COMPLETED` invoices. The list always has 52 items for the weeks 1 to 52; weeks without invoices have `average: 0` and `amount: 0`. _(source)_

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: The year to report on. Default: the current year. The spec says the default is `2022`. The code doesn't validate it. _(source)_

200.schemaRaw: AverageSalesPerWeekRow[]   // see Data Models; always 52 items, week 1 to 52

endpoint.title: Login
endpoint.description: Returns a JWT for the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. Accounts with two-factor auth (TOTP) get a restricted temporary token instead, which is exchanged for a full token by sending it back with the TOTP code. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Register
endpoint.description: Creates a customer account (role `user`). _(source)_

endpoint.title: Forgot password
endpoint.description: Sets the account's password to `welcome02`. No email confirmation or token is involved. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Change password
endpoint.description: Changes the current user's password. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Current user
endpoint.description: Profile of the user the token belongs to. `role`, `enabled` and `failed_login_attempts` are returned only when the caller is an admin. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Logout
endpoint.description: Invalidates (blacklists) the token. Later requests with it get `401`. _(verified)_

endpoint.title: Refresh token
endpoint.description: Returns a new token for the one in the `Authorization` header and invalidates the old one. An expired token can still be refreshed within the refresh window (`JWT_REFRESH_TTL`, 60 minutes by default). This route has no auth middleware; the token is read by the handler. _(source)_

endpoint.title: List users
endpoint.description: Lists customer accounts (role `user` only), 15 per page. Admin only. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Search users
endpoint.description: Searches customer accounts (role `user` only) by first name, last name, email and city. Any logged-in user can search (see Notes). Returns 15 per page. _(source)_

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Search term. The spec marks it required; without it every customer matches.

endpoint.title: Search users (HTTP QUERY)
endpoint.description: Same as `GET /users/search`, with the criteria in a JSON body. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Get user
endpoint.description: Returns a user. A non-admin can only get their own record. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Update user
endpoint.description: Updates a user's profile. A non-admin can only update their own record; only an admin can send `role`. `password` is ignored (use change-password). _(source)_

endpoint.title: Partially update user
endpoint.description: Updates only the validated fields that are sent. A non-admin can only patch their own record. _(source)_

endpoint.title: Delete user
endpoint.description: Deletes a user. Admin only. _(source)_
